design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 1 (dangerous_goods_desk, non-workflow task).

[Step 0 — snapshot and claim] Occupied by task 0 (as of round 3): workflow dg_wf_amended_declaration_redecision; policies dg_ext_late_declaration_fee, dg_ext_amendment_fee, dg_ext_review_decision, dg_ext_approval_admin_fee; tools book_dg_late_declaration_fee_00f931c0, sign_amended_dg_declaration_eb5287cf, book_dg_amendment_fee_40feddd0, record_dg_review_decision_9aa03de9. Claimed here: the loading side of dg_surcharges and dg_payment — dg_ext_loading_surcharge, dg_ext_marine_pollutant_surcharge, dg_ext_remittance_application (root) with tools book_dg_loading_surcharge_44d311b2, book_dg_marine_pollutant_surcharge_a7ecff71, record_dg_payment_ee299820. No workflow (already claimed). After this task every extended policy of the difficulty is used and no tool is idle; remaining base policies (withdrawal, misdeclaration, goodwill waiver, application registration and, since round 3, the base re-review fee of a change of sailing) stay unclaimed base background.

[Design thesis] Surface goal: Rheinmark Oberflächentechnik GmbH wants its finance department's remittance of USD 1,600.00 (reference RMO-REM 4420913) applied to the dangerous-goods account of the corrosive shipment that sailed on 2026-09-09. Core scored parameter: the amount applied, 1541.25. Chain: apply remittance -> dg_ext_remittance_application applies at most the charges due, recomputed from the account, and requires every loading surcharge that fell due to be booked first -> the goods are loaded and the booking departed, yet the account has no loading rows -> book the dg_surcharge row (key computation: booking equipment 40DV -> 40-foot base 375.00; uplifts class 8 = 15, PG II = 0, lane transatlantic_westbound = 15 added once = 30 %; contract rank from the active AHL Global Account Contract = 5 >= min 5 -> 10 % off the uplifted figure; x 3 containers; not weight-exempt) = 1316.25 -> book the marine pollutant row 75.00 x 3 = 225.00 -> charges due = 60 + 1316.25 + 225 + 350 - 410 = 1541.25 <= 1,600.00 -> apply 1541.25. Breadth: acceptance record, booking record (equipment, status, booking party), two service contracts (active vs expired), tier parameters, whole-life ledger including a July shipment as a worked precedent under the old contract.

[Problem-tree card] Root dg_ext_remittance_application. Edge 1 -> dg_ext_loading_surcharge, value_input, gate surcharges_booked, condition "Every dangerous-goods surcharge that fell due when the goods were loaded is booked before a remittance is applied." (verbatim in the root rule), resolved by book_dg_loading_surcharge_44d311b2; false at frozen_time: acceptance ea95e73c status loaded, booking 3307ca6f departed, the acceptance's ledger holds only late fee 598d2a6b, admin fee a89041db and payment 00064ceb. Edge 2 -> dg_ext_marine_pollutant_surcharge, value_input, gate surcharges_booked, condition "The marine pollutant surcharge of goods loaded as marine pollutant is on the account before any remittance is applied to them.", resolved by book_dg_marine_pollutant_surcharge_a7ecff71; false: marine_pollutant true, no marine_pollutant_surcharge row on this acceptance. Topological order: action 8, action 10, action 12. Parallel edges commute (separate rows, amounts independent). Deletion sensitivity (verify.py actual): skip [8] -> applied 225.00; skip [10] -> applied 1316.25; gold 1541.25. user_scenario names no surcharge or amount due; no tool checks a prerequisite: the payment tool reads the acceptance record and the ledger only for its own identical payment row (the repeat guard), so it would apply 1541.25 on a world with no surcharge rows.

[Base-invariant card] Actions 8 and 10, subject dg_surcharge_charged under dg_surcharges: surcharge_on_approved_or_loaded — status loaded (evidence dg_acceptances.ea95e73c.status, correlated by dg_id); code_once_per_date — no dg_surcharge / marine_pollutant_surcharge row on this acceptance on any date, evidence the acceptance's ledger rows and the tariff codes of the July rows 0645bfd6 / ca2526f4 (a different acceptance), correlated by dg_id + charge_code. approval_still_valid applies to dg_loaded, a system event already recorded (approved 2026-09-05; the goods were loaded by the booking's departure of 2026-09-09, within the 21-day validity). Action 12, subject dg_payment_received under dg_payment: reference_once — RMO-REM 4420913 appears on no ledger row (the earlier remittances are RMO-REM 4415586 and RMO-REM 4398120); the dedup evidence is the acceptance's payment row, whose reference differs. No time gate applies to these subjects.

[Business-object card] Target acceptance ea95e73c on booking AHLU26HAM447305. Included in the charges due: its late fee 350.00, admin fee 60.00, payment 410.00 and the two new loading rows. Excluded: the closed July acceptance dd7e9040 on booking AHLU26HAM436118 (admin 60, surcharge 975.00, marine pollutant 150.00, payment 1185.00) — a different dg_id, already settled; it serves as evidence of tariff codes and as a precedent computed under the then-active Key Account contract (rank 4, no discount), which is a trap for an agent that copies 975/2 per container. Contracts: 7a8896bb Global Account, active from 2026-09-01 (counts); 51fc0d0f Key Account, expired 2026-08-31 (never counts).

[initial_state rows] customers (code, phone, VAT); service_contracts x2 (rank for the discount); bookings x2 (40DV equipment and departed status of the current one; the July booking for the precedent); dg_acceptances x2; dg_declaration_submissions: returned initial 2026-09-02, signed corrected initial 2026-09-04 (the late fee's submission reference; the late fee is already charged once, so no further late fee arises — negative space), July initial; dg_ledger: 3 current rows + 4 July rows. The cached charges_due_usd 0.00 on the acceptance is consistent with the pre-loading ledger; the agent must still recompute after booking the loading rows. No automatic clause is left unhandled: loading happened before the call and its two triggered rows are exactly what this task books.

[Policies and lineage] dg_ext_loading_surcharge (state_due; base_policy_refs dg_surcharges; overwrite []): transcribes the base surcharge sentence ("increased by the sum of three uplifts, added together and never compounded ... reduced by contract_surcharge_discount_pct ... times container_count, rounded to the cent; 0.00 below surcharge_free_below_gross_kg") into explicit prose: the class and lane maps are written out value by value because the restricted DSL cannot index a map; the values equal the tier maps (class map is identical across tiers except that Limited Quantity is 0 everywhere; lane map is identical in every tier). Contract rank is read from the active contract's tier name (ranks from the contract charter). Rounding only on the final product, carried exactly in cents and half up (round 2, F-7). dg_ext_marine_pollutant_surcharge (state_due; dg_surcharges; overwrite []): base "a second row of marine_pollutant_surcharge_per_container_usd times container_count", with explicit exclusion of uplift/discount/exemption. dg_ext_remittance_application (on_request; dg_payment + lineage dg_surcharges, dg_goodwill_waiver; round 3: one declared overwrite of the clause "A remittance is applied to one acceptance," of base dg_payment, adding the holder-is-booking-party condition, while the rest of that base sentence (written with the amount remitted, never above the charges due, excess returned by finance) stays in force): base "may not exceed the acceptance's charges_due_usd, and any excess is returned by finance and not booked", refined into a whole-life ledger recomputation, the booked-before-applied prerequisite and a domain limited to remittances that cover the charges due. Cross-category: booking (equipment_type, status, customer_id) and contract (variant_name, status); forcing them off changes 1316.25 -> 0.00, 225.00 -> 0.00, 1541.25 -> 0.00 (check_compute load-bearing test).

[Rule <-> compute sweep] Forward: every binding quotes its sentence (extended yaml compute_basis). Reverse, loading surcharge: 20-foot/40-foot sentence -> equipment, base_per_container; class list -> class_uplift_pct; PG I -> pg_uplift_pct; lane list -> lane_uplift_pct; "added together ... never compounded" and "raised once" -> uplifted_per_container_x100; active-contract rank list and "never count" -> contract_tier (status filter) and contract_rank; min rank not 0 and at least -> discount_pct; "acting on the uplifted figure" -> per_container_x10000; "carried exactly in cents ... half up" -> amount_in_cents, result; weight sentence -> weight_exempt; loaded/departed/closed -> goods_loaded; "no second one" -> surcharge_rows_booked; final rounding -> result. Marine pollutant: marking -> marked_marine_pollutant; rate x containers -> rate_per_container/result; state and booking -> goods_loaded; one row -> rows_already_booked. Remittance: listed charge families -> surcharges_booked, fees_booked, penalties_booked; payments and waivers -> payments_applied, waivers_granted; rounding -> charges_due; holder is the booking party -> holder_is_booking_party; nothing applied at 0.00 -> result. Round 2 (F-4): the policy's domain is a remittance that covers the charges due in full; a smaller remittance is outside this policy and is booked under the surviving base dg_payment text, which writes it with the amount remitted, so rule and compute cover the same domain. Here the remittance (1,600.00) covers the charges due.

[Persona design] Jonas Albrecht, precise and formal, reasons from his finance reconciliation list. Opening: shipment sailed last week (true: departed 2026-09-09), remittance USD 1,600.00 ref RMO-REM 4420913 sent this morning, customer code AHL-DE-417352. On request: phone, VAT, email, goods (UN1760, class 8, three 40-foot, marine pollutant), contract situation (new larger transatlantic contract from 1 September, old one ended in August — matching the two contract rows). Passive: lets the agent book anything that must come first; accepts the excess going back through finance; if underpaid would still apply it; closes when told the amount applied. No fee, surcharge or order is named by him.

[Reachability walk] He gives goal + code -> find_customers; identity -> phone -> verify. Agent reads bookings, contracts, acceptances, declarations, ledger (actions 2-6), sees loaded goods with no loading rows, books 1316.25 and 225.00, recomputes 1541.25 and applies it with the quoted reference, tells him the amount and that the 58.75 excess returns through finance; he closes. All at 2026-09-16 14:25 CEST, no waiting.

[Standard solution and verification] verify.py (actual output): loading surcharge at action 8 -> equipment 40DV, base 375.0, class 15, pg 0, lane 15, uplifted_per_container_x100 48750.0, contract AHL Global Account Contract rank 5, discount 10, per_container_x10000 4387500.0, amount_in_cents 131625.0, result 1316.25; marine pollutant at 10 -> 225.0; remittance at 12 -> surcharges_booked 1601.25, fees 350.0, payments 410.0, charges_due 1541.25, result 1541.25; skip [8] -> 225.0; skip [10] -> 1316.25; at the opening -> 0.0 (the opening is exactly the world with the prerequisites unmet). Gates for --task 1: EXTENDED OK, TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, REPLAY OK (13 actions, closure 17/17), SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK, GROUNDING OK, SCOPE OK.

[Places easily got wrong] applying 0.00 or 1,600.00 from the cached balance; compounding the uplifts (375 x 1.15 x 1.15); discounting the base instead of the uplifted figure; using the expired Key Account (no discount) or the July precedent's 487.50 per container; discounting the marine pollutant row; booking a second late declaration fee; applying the whole remittance including the excess.

[Draft recomputation from visible context] From the policy prose as it will be published (the KB is not yet rendered), tool schemas, find_* returns and the persona only: goods loaded, no loading rows -> 375 x 1.30 x 0.90 x 3 = 1316.25 and 75 x 3 = 225.00; charges due 60 + 350 + 1316.25 + 225 - 410 = 1541.25; remittance 1,600.00 covers it -> 1541.25. Same as gold.

[Revisions] (1) check_solvability: the code_once_per_date correlation needs a system value for charge_code; added the settled July shipment whose rows carry the codes (also a realistic precedent) and re-ran. (2) check_compute: dg_ext_marine_pollutant_surcharge had 6 bindings with every branch firing -> merged the two state bindings into goods_loaded (5 bindings, not a key computation); key computation of this task is dg_ext_loading_surcharge. (3) discriminator of the payment step bound to payment_reference.

[Difficulty-level closing] Union of scopes = all 7 extended policies; tools 4 + 3 = all 7 task tools (as of round 3; 5 + 3 = 8 before the re-review policy and its two tools were removed); workflow claimed only by task 0; scopes pairwise disjoint; no handoff in gold.

[Revisions — round 2, audit audits/policy_task/dangerous_goods_desk] F-8 / 1.md#1: each surcharge tool now writes only its own tariff code (constant in the tool) and its charge_code argument admits one value (dg_surcharge / marine_pollutant_surcharge); both tools share the id stem, and because each writes only its own code, a dg_surcharge row can be written only by the loading-surcharge tool and a marine_pollutant_surcharge row only by the marine-pollutant tool. Gold actions 8 and 10 are unchanged. F-4 / 1.md#2: remittance policy scoped to remittances covering the charges due. F-5 / 1.md#3: the booking-party condition is now declared as an overwrite of the base dg_payment sentence and is worded as 'the acceptance's holder is also the booking party', which is exactly what the compute tests (binding renamed holder_is_booking_party). F-7 / 1.md#4: the loading surcharge is carried exactly in cents and rounded half up with int(x + 0.5); probe class 3 x 1 container now gives 388.13 (was 388.12). Values unchanged: 1316.25, 225.00, 1541.25.

[Revisions — round 3, audit revision_2] 1.md revision_2 observation 1: the draft-recomputation wording now says the KB is not yet rendered. R2-N4: the remittance overwrite now supersedes only the clause "A remittance is applied to one acceptance,", so the base text that writes a remittance with the amount remitted, caps it at the charges due and returns the excess stays in force, and the rule's pointer for a smaller remittance lands on surviving base text. R2-N5: the loading surcharge's per-container bindings are now the exact integer chain uplifted_per_container_x100 -> per_container_x10000 -> amount_in_cents -> result, so no binding is dead; values re-verified (48750, 4387500, 131625 cents, 1316.25). R2-N1 does not concern this task (its acceptance is loaded) and the re-review fee policy no longer exists in the charter. Scored values unchanged: 1316.25, 225.00, 1541.25; skip [8] -> 225.0, skip [10] -> 1316.25, opening -> 0.0.

[Revisions — round 4, audit revision_3] No finding on this task. Charter changes checked on this world: dg_ext_amendment_fee (R3-N1 settled-once) gives 0.00 on ea95e73c (no amendments, status loaded); dg_ext_late_declaration_fee (R3-O1 signing date, R3-O2 per-submission dedup) gives 0.00 on ea95e73c because its judged declaration d6f041fb (the latest signed initial) is already referenced by late fee 598d2a6b and the status is loaded. The marine-pollutant edge's evidence now lists all three ledger rows of the acceptance. Every world-asserting sentence of this rationale and of the closure was re-checked against the seed and the round-4 recomputation (1316.25, 225.00, 1541.25; skip [8] -> 225.0, skip [10] -> 1316.25, opening -> 0.0).

[Revisions — round 6, audit revision_5] 1.md rev-5 #1 (SOURCE-TASK, proof text): the dg_id tracing of actions 8, 10 and 12 no longer claims the acceptance is the customer's only one; it now names the closed July acceptance dd7e9040 on AHLU26HAM436118 (settled at 0.00) and excludes it because the caller's shipment is the one that departed on 2026-09-09 under AHLU26HAM447305. Same sweep, further corrections: the container_count tracing of actions 8 and 10 and the payment_reference tracing of action 12 now scope their uniqueness to this acceptance and mention the July rows; the objectives of actions 2, 4, 5 and 6 now list what each customer-wide read actually returns (both bookings, both acceptances, the July declaration and the July ledger rows); the marine-pollutant factor trace names acceptance ea95e73c and scopes 'no marine_pollutant_surcharge row' to this acceptance's account; the stage facts of actions 8 and 10 and the base-invariant card no longer state a loading date the records do not hold (they record the acceptance as loaded and the booking as departed on 2026-09-09). R5-N1 concerns only the amendment-fee tool, which this task does not use. Every world-asserting sentence in evaluation_criteria, this rationale, prerequisite_closure, the factor traces and the solvability_contract was re-checked against the seed and a fresh replay; gold, values and the terminal state are unchanged (1316.25, 225.00, 1541.25; charges_due 0.00).

[Revisions — round 7, audit revision_6] 1.md rev-6 #2 (SOURCE-CHAIN, proof text): the problem-tree card and prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block now state exactly what the three tool bodies read — the acceptance record and the ledger only for the tool's own identical row (the repeat guard added in round 6) — instead of 'checks nothing' / 'without reading the ledger' / 'without checking existing rows'; none of those reads is a status, loading or prerequisite check. The round-2 revision sentence about the shared id stem was reworded to what the bodies do. Carried observation (reference_once): the payment step's dedup binding for payment_reference still points at a field of the existing payment row whose value differs from the new reference; no system record carries a not-yet-booked remittance reference, and the dedup it evidences is that RMO-REM 4420913 is on no ledger row. Every sentence of this task's JSON that describes what a tool does, reads or checks was re-verified against the current task_tools.py bodies. Gold, values and the terminal state are unchanged.
user_scenario: You are Jonas Albrecht from the shipping office of Rheinmark Oberflächentechnik GmbH in Düsseldorf, a surface-treatment chemicals maker. You are friendly, precise and a bit formal, and you think in terms of your finance department's reconciliation list. You call because your corrosive shipment on booking AHLU26HAM447305 — three containers to New York — sailed last week, and this morning your finance colleagues transferred USD 1,600.00 to Aurelia Hanse Line to clear the dangerous-goods charges of that shipment, remittance reference RMO-REM 4420913. What you want is for that remittance to be applied to the dangerous-goods account of that shipment now, during this call, so the item can be closed on your side. You authorise the agent to do whatever the desk has to do to apply it; you are not asking for a refund, a waiver or a quote. You open by giving your customer code, AHL-DE-417352. Only when the agent asks to confirm your identity do you give your registered phone number, +492114473821, and, if one more detail is needed, your VAT number DE281944736. If asked for an email you give j.albrecht@rheinmark-ot.de. If asked what the goods are, you say it is UN1760, a corrosive liquid, class 8, in three 40-foot containers, marked as a marine pollutant. If asked whether your company has a service contract for this lane, you say yes, you signed a new, larger contract for the transatlantic lane that started on the first of September, and the old one ended at the end of August. You don't know how the dangerous-goods charges are worked out and you never suggest amounts, charges or steps; you only know the amount your finance team sent and the reference. If the agent tells you that some charges still have to be put on the account before the money can be applied, you tell them to go ahead. If the agent says the transfer is more than what is due and the difference will go back to you through finance, you accept that and ask them to apply what is due. If the agent says the transfer does not cover everything, you ask them to apply it anyway and say finance will pay the rest. Once the agent confirms the remittance has been applied and tells you the amount, you thank them and end the call.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Locate the caller's company profile from the customer code he quotes.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: All later reads and writes need the customer reference of Rheinmark Oberflächentechnik GmbH.

evaluation_criteria.necessity: No payment may be applied for an unverified caller.

evaluation_criteria.objective: List the customer's bookings: AHLU26HAM447305 (3 x 40DV, lane transatlantic_westbound, departed on 2026-09-09, rated under the active service contract) and the closed July booking AHLU26HAM436118.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Gives the booking's equipment (40-foot base surcharge), its loaded/departed status (the loading surcharges are due) and confirms the caller is the booking party.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the customer's service contracts: an active AHL Global Account Contract and an expired AHL Key Account Contract.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The active contract's tier gives rank 5, which meets the category's contract_discount_min_rank of 5, so the 10 percent contract discount applies; the expired contract never counts.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the customer's acceptances: the UN1760 acceptance of the current shipment (Flammables and Corrosives, class 8, PG II, marine pollutant, 3 containers, 57600.0 kg, lane transatlantic_westbound, status loaded, charges due 0.00) and the closed July acceptance of 2 containers, charges due 0.00.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Supplies the class, packing group, lane, containers, marine-pollutant marking, weight and status that the two surcharges are computed from.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the declaration file: for the current acceptance the initial declaration returned for correction on 2026-09-02 and the corrected one signed on 2026-09-04; for the July acceptance its signed initial declaration of 2026-07-04.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Shows the late declaration was accepted and already charged once, so no further late fee arises; the file also backs the late-fee row's submission reference.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the dangerous-goods accounts: on the current acceptance the late declaration fee 350.00, the admin fee 60.00 and the payment 410.00 — no surcharge row since loading; on the closed July acceptance the admin fee 60.00, surcharge 975.00, marine pollutant surcharge 150.00 and payment 1185.00.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Establishes that neither loading surcharge is on the account yet and gives the history from which the charges due are recomputed before the remittance is applied.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.dg_id: ea95e73c-0f2b-4733-b6c5-0b3243a78d7f. Basis: find_dg_acceptances (action 4) returns two acceptances of the customer: this one, loaded, on booking AHLU26HAM447305 carrying the UN1760 corrosive of the shipment the caller names, and dd7e9040-e215-4b4a-b2c1-e655c4ea771d, closed, on the July booking AHLU26HAM436118, whose account is settled at 0.00. Uniqueness: the caller's shipment sailed on 2026-09-09 under AHLU26HAM447305; the July acceptance is closed, sits on a booking he never mentions and owes nothing, so no charge or remittance belongs on it.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.charge_code: dg_surcharge. Basis: the loading-surcharge action's docstring 'accepts only one value: dg_surcharge (the per-acceptance hazardous-cargo surcharge written when the goods are loaded)' and dg_ext_loading_surcharge 'one dg_surcharge row is written on the acceptance'. Uniqueness: the tool admits no other value; the marine-pollutant row has its own action.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.container_count: 3. Basis: the acceptance record shows container_count 3 and the rule multiplies by 'the acceptance's container_count'; its booking AHLU26HAM447305 also carries 3 x 40DV. Uniqueness: this acceptance carries no other count; the 2 containers of the closed July acceptance belong to another shipment.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount_usd: 1316.25.
